The client's `case_id` is replaced by a server-issued ULID: an id that a client
can choose is an id a client can collide with or forge.

`buyer_contact` is accepted so the caller can draft the acceptance invite, and is

schema, and persisting personal data needs a DPDP decision the repo has not

post.description:
Select a bid, sign the DEMO consent, and move to AWAITING_ESIGN.

The consent document is built here, hashed, and its hash is what the eSign
provider is asked to sign, so the signed copy can be checked against what was
shown. The PDF is watermarked TEMPLATE and every party is fictional.

Ask the buyer to accept the invoice, then follow the provider's decision.

The buyer acts in their own login: nothing moves until they accept. This route
applies `request_buyer_acceptance`, polls the provider once, and applies
`buyer_accepted` when it has happened. The polling is a stand-in for the signed
webhooks in `docs/webhooks.md`, which do not exist yet.
Cancel before signature. After signature the receivable is the financier's.

get.description: The case's payment history, including voided rows (never deleted).

post.description:
Record a payment, re-evaluate through the engine, and audit it.

The engine already has a payment input (`transaction.part_payments`), so a
payment is appended there with a `v5:<payment_id>` reference and the case is
re-evaluated. The v5 `payments` row remains the source of truth; voiding
removes only the matching engine-input entry and keeps the row.

A payment cannot be future-dated, cannot precede the invoice, and cannot take
the total above the engine's remaining claim (invoice amount plus interest
accrued so far). A financed invoice's receivable belongs to the financier,
so payments to the supplier are refused with 409.

Void a payment without deleting it, then re-evaluate through the engine.

The row keeps its amount and gains `voided_at`; the engine input loses only
the matching `v5:<payment_id>` entry. Repeating the call is a no-op and
writes no second event.

Prepare a stage's draft and move the track to `STAGE_n_PREPARED`.

Preparing is not sending: the response carries the draft and nothing leaves the
server.

Record that the owner sent this stage from their own client.

The event stores the channel so the trail is honest about how it went out, and the
wording stays "the owner says they sent it" â€” the server has no way to know.

Record that the owner filed on the ODR portal.

A separate action from `mark-sent` because filing is a different claim: the pack
being ready is not the same as the owner having submitted it. This is the only
path to `ODR_FILED_BY_OWNER`.

Days to pay are measured from the engine's day of acceptance and "on time"

post.description:
Fold a PROVISIONAL customer's invoices into another customer.

Same-PAN registrations already group automatically. This is the owner
confirming that a name-only or unformatted record is the same buyer. A
customer that already has its own PAN is refused: different PANs are never
merged, and the two can be linked as a group instead. The provisional row is
kept with no invoices, which is what makes `detach` an exact undo.

Separate invoices or a GSTIN from a customer. The undo for `attach`.

When the invoice was moved by an `attach`, the detach restores the exact
customer it came from. Otherwise the invoice gets its own provisional record,
resolved from its own buyer details. Either way the move is audited on the
invoice's chain and can be reversed by attaching again.

Attach one registration to a customer, audited on every affected invoice.

A GSTIN that carries a PAN promotes a provisional customer to that PAN. A
GSTIN belonging to a different PAN is refused: different PANs are never
merged, and the two customers can be linked as a group instead.

post.description: Evaluate a case with the real engine (sections 6.1-6.6).

Extract machine-suggested candidates from an uploaded text file (B9).

Regex and keyword first, offline: a WhatsApp .txt export is parsed into
messages and tagged, invoice and PO text yields labelled fields - each with
a line citation and a confidence - and a human confirms them into a
`CaseEvaluationRequest` before anything is evaluated (nothing here calls the
engine, and the engine never calls this module).

Environment flags, read per request and never at import time:

- `EXTRACTION_DEMO_CACHE=1` returns the prepared result stored for that
  exact text, with no network at all.
- `EXTRACTION_LLM=1` plus `EXTRACTION_LLM_URL` enables the optional LLM
  layer, which only fills fields the regex path could not read; any failure
  falls back to the regex result untouched.

The objection window comes from the statute config (the tagger holds no
statutory number of its own); when it is absent, lateness is reported as
*not assessed* rather than as "zero days".

Draft one artifact for this case (section 8.1).

The case is evaluated first, so the draft is filled from the engine's own
figures rather than from anything the client sends (golden rule 7). When the
stage cannot be produced - the gate stopped the case, or a figure the draft
needs was never computed - the response still carries markdown: an honest
note saying why that stage is unavailable, never a half-filled document.
Nothing is sent anywhere; the PDF is optional and its failure degrades to
markdown plus a `warnings[]` entry rather than an error.

post.description:
Preview an invoice-history CSV, or commit the file you previewed.

Columns: `invoice_no*, invoice_date*, delivery_date*, amount*, buyer_name*,
buyer_gstin, agreed_credit_days, paid_on, paid_amount, notes`. Dates are
`YYYY-MM-DD` or `DD-MM-YYYY` for the whole file; amounts may use Indian
grouping (`1,25,000.00`). A cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is
refused (CSV injection guard). Every error says which row and which column,
in plain English.

`preview` stores nothing at all. `commit` requires the token it returned plus
the same bytes, creates each case through the same function `POST /cases`
uses (so the engine runs per row and the customer is attached), records a
payment when `paid_on` and `paid_amount` are present, and skips an invoice
that is already in the book.

Split a settlement offer against this case's own numbers (section 8.1).

The claim is evaluated first, so the split always uses the engine's figures

with the buyer-cost lines, and nothing is assumed about time value.
